sample_unit: case variants (30 physician-authored rheumatology vignettes, each rephrased three times)
models_evaluated: OpenAI LLM (five LLMs from three providers; specific model names not reported in text)

links.outcome: Change in AI triage concordance when patient race/ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and language barrier were varied
links.effect: Race or ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and language barrier produced no detectable effect, including in mixed-effects models accounting for repeated vignette use; framing cues (anxious, anchoring) did shift outputs.
links.quote: In contrast, race or ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and language barrier produced no detectable effect, including in mixed-effects models that accounted for repeated vignette use.

links.outcome: Change in concordance with expert ground truth under framing perturbations
links.effect: Baseline concordance 0.869; clinician anchoring reduced concordance, significantly for acuity (dismissive anchor, vignette-level p = 0.01), mainly by downgrading urgency.
links.quote: Clinician anchoring in the referral note reduced concordance, consistently across models and rephrasings and significantly for acuity (dismissive anchor, vignette-level p = 0.01), mainly by downgrading urgency.

links.outcome: Attribution of symptoms to psychological vs organic causes when patient described as anxious
links.effect: Models attributed symptoms to psychological causes 13.1% vs 4.5% at baseline; odds ratio 3.2 versus stoic framing.
links.quote: When patients were described as anxious, models attributed symptoms to psychological rather than organic causes nearly three times as often as at baseline (13.1% vs 4.5%; odds ratio 3.2 versus stoic framing), a shift that risks relabeling organic disease as functional.

unlisted_practices: Separate objective clinical evidence from interpretive framing in AI-assisted triage inputs
Treat urgency and psychological attribution as auditable safety signals

screen.reason: The study evaluates LLM performance and bias/sensitivity in rheumatology triage using simulated clinical vignettes across various demographic and framing cues, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
